name: Reflow
explanation: This criterion requires that content can reflow into a single column at narrow viewport widths without forcing the user to scroll in two directions to read it. At a viewport 320 CSS pixels wide, roughly what you get zooming a 1280px-wide design to 400%, the page must still work with only vertical scrolling. In practice this means a responsive layout: columns stack, sidebars move below or collapse, and fixed-width elements give way to fluid ones. There are specific exceptions for content that genuinely needs two-dimensional layout, like data tables, maps, and images — those are allowed to require scrolling in both directions. This is different from SC 1.4.4 Resize Text, which is about 200% browser zoom preserving readability generally. This criterion is specifically about reflow at 320px and banning two-dimensional scrolling for ordinary content.
whoItAffects: People with low vision who use high browser zoom levels, often 300-400%, rather than a screen magnifier — magnifiers already pan in two dimensions, but zoomed browser content shouldn't force that extra effort. It affects people with physical or motor disabilities who find horizontal scrolling significantly harder than vertical scrolling, particularly anyone using a switch device where tracking a scroll position in two axes at once is error-prone. It also affects anyone reading on a small device, like a phone in portrait orientation or a screen split with another app, where a layout that assumes desktop width becomes unusable rather than merely cramped.
howToTest: Open the page in a desktop browser and use the browser's device toolbar mode to set the viewport to exactly 320 CSS pixels wide. Alternatively, zoom a standard 1280px-wide layout to 400%. Then scroll through the entire page using only vertical scrolling, and check whether you ever need to scroll sideways to read a sentence or reach a button. A horizontal scrollbar for genuinely two-dimensional content, like a wide data table, is acceptable. A horizontal scrollbar needed to read ordinary paragraph text or a form is a failure. Also check that no content is cut off or overlapping as the layout reflows.

check.question: A page requires horizontal scrolling to read body text when the viewport is set to 320 CSS pixels wide. Which of these is true about SC 1.4.10 Reflow?
choices: This is always acceptable because some horizontal scrolling is expected on narrow screens
This is a failure, because ordinary content must reflow to avoid two-dimensional scrolling at 320px width
This is only a concern if the user is also using a screen reader
This is acceptable as long as the content is technically readable by scrolling in both directions
